- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for downward momentum.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% in the following 3–5 periods.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3+ consecutive periods, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward recent 5-day average, especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 5 days, assume lagged reaction — adjust forecast to align with 7–10 day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 20–30% after sentiment drop.
